1	# Sorting
2	
3	A small, well-factored sorting package, grown from a single procedural
4	`bubble_sort.java` file into a set of interchangeable algorithms behind one
5	Strategy interface.
6	
7	## Structure
8	
9	All sources live in the `sorting` package:
10	
11	| File                     | Responsibility                                                       |
12	|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
13	| `Sorter.java`            | Strategy interface for in-place, comparator-driven sorting.         |
14	| `SortObserver.java`      | Hook notified of each comparison and swap (default no-ops).         |
15	| `SortStats.java`         | `SortObserver` that counts comparisons and swaps.                   |
16	| `IntComparator.java`     | Primitive `int` comparison function (no boxing).                    |
17	| `BubbleSort.java`        | Bubble sort (early-exit optimized): generic + primitive `int[]`.    |
18	| `InsertionSort.java`     | Insertion sort: O(n) on nearly-sorted input, stable.                |
19	| `MergeSort.java`         | Top-down merge sort: O(n log n) always, stable.                     |
20	| `QuickSort.java`         | In-place quicksort: median-of-three pivot, O(log n) stack.          |
21	| `SortSupport.java`       | Package-private shared helpers (element swap, argument checks).      |
22	| `IntArrayFormatter.java` | Formats `int[]` for display, separate from the algorithm and I/O.   |
23	| `SortingDemo.java`       | `main` entry point; demonstrates swapping strategies.               |
24	| `SortingTest.java`       | Dependency-free test harness; non-zero exit on failure.             |
25	
26	## Algorithms
27	
28	Every algorithm implements `Sorter`, so client code picks one at runtime and
29	sorts any object type with any `Comparator`:
30	
31	```java
32	Sorter sorter = new MergeSort();        // or BubbleSort / InsertionSort / QuickSort
33	sorter.sort(values);                    // natural order
34	sorter.sort(values, Comparator.reverseOrder());
35	```
36	
37	| Algorithm   | Best     | Average    | Worst      | Stable | Extra space |
38	|-------------|----------|------------|------------|--------|-------------|
39	| Bubble      | O(n)     | O(n²)      | O(n²)      | yes    | O(1)        |
40	| Insertion   | O(n)     | O(n²)      | O(n²)      | yes    | O(1)        |
41	| Merge       | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | yes | O(n)        |
42	| Quick       | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n²)    | no     | O(log n)    |
43	
44	`BubbleSort` additionally offers an allocation-free primitive `int[]` path with
45	an `IntComparator` — something the JDK's `Arrays.sort(int[])` cannot do.
46	
47	## Instrumentation
48	
49	Every generic sort accepts an optional `SortObserver`, notified of each
50	comparison and swap. `SortStats` is a ready-made counting observer:
51	
52	```java
53	SortStats stats = new SortStats();
54	new BubbleSort().sort(values, Comparator.naturalOrder(), stats);
55	System.out.println(stats);   // e.g. "21 comparisons, 14 swaps"
56	```
57	
58	This makes algorithmic behavior observable and testable — for instance, bubble
59	sort on already-sorted input reports `n-1` comparisons and zero swaps (its
60	early exit), whereas reverse input costs `n(n-1)/2` of each. Insertion and merge
61	sort shift/copy rather than swap, so they report zero swaps. The observer
62	defaults to `SortObserver.NO_OP`, which the two- and one-argument `sort`
63	overloads use, so the uninstrumented path carries no overhead. The primitive
64	`int[]` paths are not instrumented.
65	
66	### History
67	
68	Refactored from the original single-file `bubble_sort.java`: separated the
69	algorithm, formatting, demo, and tests; made the algorithm generic and
70	comparator-driven; gave the primitive path comparator symmetry; then added the
71	insertion/merge/quick implementations behind the `Sorter` interface. The
72	original primitive bubble-sort output is still reproduced by `SortingDemo`.
73	
74	## Build & run
75	
76	```sh
77	javac sorting/*.java
78	
79	java sorting.SortingDemo   # run the demo
80	java sorting.SortingTest   # run the tests
81	```
82

# Sorting

A small, well-factored sorting package, grown from a single procedural
`bubble_sort.java` file into a set of interchangeable algorithms behind one
Strategy interface.

## Structure

All sources live in the `sorting` package:

| File                     | Responsibility                                                       |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Sorter.java`            | Strategy interface for in-place, comparator-driven sorting.         |
| `SortObserver.java`      | Hook notified of each comparison and swap (default no-ops).         |
| `SortStats.java`         | `SortObserver` that counts comparisons and swaps.                   |
| `IntComparator.java`     | Primitive `int` comparison function (no boxing).                    |
| `BubbleSort.java`        | Bubble sort (early-exit optimized): generic + primitive `int[]`.    |
| `InsertionSort.java`     | Insertion sort: O(n) on nearly-sorted input, stable.                |
| `MergeSort.java`         | Top-down merge sort: O(n log n) always, stable.                     |
| `QuickSort.java`         | In-place quicksort: median-of-three pivot, O(log n) stack.          |
| `SortSupport.java`       | Package-private shared helpers (element swap, argument checks).      |
| `IntArrayFormatter.java` | Formats `int[]` for display, separate from the algorithm and I/O.   |
| `SortingDemo.java`       | `main` entry point; demonstrates swapping strategies.               |
| `SortingTest.java`       | Dependency-free test harness; non-zero exit on failure.             |

## Algorithms

Every algorithm implements `Sorter`, so client code picks one at runtime and
sorts any object type with any `Comparator`:

```java
Sorter sorter = new MergeSort();        // or BubbleSort / InsertionSort / QuickSort
sorter.sort(values);                    // natural order
sorter.sort(values, Comparator.reverseOrder());
```

# Sorting

`bubble_sort.java` file into a set of interchangeable algorithms behind one
Strategy interface.

## Structure

| `IntArrayFormatter.java` | Formats `int[]` for display, separate from the algorithm and I/O.   |

| `SortingTest.java`       | Dependency-free test harness; non-zero exit on failure.             |

## Algorithms

Every algorithm implements `Sorter`, so client code picks one at runtime and
sorts any object type with any `Comparator`:


defaults to `SortObserver.NO_OP`, which the two- and one-argument `sort`
overloads use, so the uninstrumented path carries no overhead. The primitive

algorithm, formatting, demo, and tests; made the algorithm generic and
comparator-driven; gave the primitive path comparator symmetry; then added the
insertion/merge/quick implementations behind the `Sorter` interface. The
original primitive bubble-sort output is still reproduced by `SortingDemo`.

